subject: Mathematics
text: Solve a one-variable linear equation by keeping both sides balanced. Remove the constant term first, then isolate the variable.

hints: First remove the constant term from both sides.
Then divide by the coefficient of x.

solution_steps: identify the variable term and constant term
remove the constant from both sides
divide both sides by the coefficient
check the value in the original equation

common_misconceptions.text: Changing only one side of the equation.
common_misconceptions.correction: Whatever operation is done to one side must also be done to the other side.

common_misconceptions.text: Treating a final numeric answer as a valid first step.
common_misconceptions.correction: Ask for the operation or equation step before accepting the final value.

teaching_sequence: ask what term should be removed first
guide the student to subtract the constant from both sides
ask the student to isolate x
only reveal the final answer after reasoning is shown or policy unlocks it

khmer_terms.linear equation: សមីការលីនេអ៊ែរ

subject: Mathematics
text: The coordinate plane uses an x-axis and y-axis. A point (x, y) tells how far to move horizontally and vertically from the origin.

examples.answer: Move 2 units right and 3 units up from the origin.
solution_steps: Positive x moves right and positive y moves up.

exercises.prompt: Where is B(-1, 4) located from the origin?
hints: Look at the sign of x first.

common_misconceptions.correction: Read coordinates in the order (x, y): horizontal first, vertical second.

common_misconceptions.text: Ignoring negative signs when locating a point.
common_misconceptions.correction: Negative x moves left and negative y moves down.

teaching_sequence: ask which number is x
ask which direction x moves
ask which number is y
connect the point to movement from the origin

khmer_terms.origin: ចំណុចកំណើត
khmer_terms.ordered pair: គូមានលំដាប់

subject: Mathematics
text: The slope between two points compares vertical change to horizontal change. Use the same point order for both changes.

examples.problem: Find the slope between A(0, 1) and B(1, 3).

exercises.prompt: Find the slope between C(2, 4) and D(5, 10).
hints: Compute change in x using the same point order.

solution_steps: divide change in y by change in x

common_misconceptions.text: Reversing the numerator and denominator in the slope formula.
common_misconceptions.correction: Slope is change in y over change in x.

common_misconceptions.text: Using different point order for x and y changes.
common_misconceptions.correction: Use the same point order in both numerator and denominator.

teaching_sequence: ask the student to label the two points
ask for change in y
ask for change in x
then simplify the ratio

khmer_terms.change in y: បម្រែបម្រួល y
khmer_terms.change in x: បម្រែបម្រួល x

subject: Mathematics
text: To find the equation of a line through two points, find the slope first, then use a point to solve for the intercept or use point-slope form.

examples.problem: Find the equation of the line through D(0, 1) and E(1, 3).
solution_steps: Use D(0, 1) in y = mx + b: 1 = 2(0) + b.
So b = 1, and the line is y = 2x + 1.

exercises.prompt: Find the equation of the line through A(1, 2) and B(3, 6).
hints: Substitute one point into y = mx + b.

solution_steps: find the slope from the two points
substitute into y = mx + b or point-slope form
solve for b if using slope-intercept form

common_misconceptions.text: Trying to write the line equation before finding slope.
common_misconceptions.correction: Always find or identify slope first.

common_misconceptions.text: Assuming the y-value of any point is the y-intercept.
common_misconceptions.correction: The y-intercept is only the y-value when x = 0.

teaching_sequence: ask for the slope first
check the slope calculation
ask which point to substitute
guide solving for the intercept
lock final equation until reasoning is shown

subject: Mathematics
subtopic: Propositions, Truth Tables, Set Operations, Intervals, Radicals & Absolute Value
text: MoEYS Grade 10 Mathematics Chapters 1–2: Mathematical Logic (តក្កវិទ្យា), Sets (សំណុំ), and Real Numbers (ចំនួនពិត). Covers propositions, negation, conjunction, disjunction, implication (P => Q), equivalence (P <=> Q), and quantifiers; set union (A U B), intersection (A cap B), set difference (A \ B), complement, and Principle of Inclusion-Exclusion n(A U B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A cap B); simplifying surds/radicals, rationalizing denominators via conjugates, and solving absolute value equations |x - a| = b and inequalities |x - a| <= b.

Compute union, intersection, set difference, and cardinality of finite sets and real intervals

concepts.title: Mathematical Logic & Implication (តក្កវិទ្យាគណិតវិទ្យា និងផលវិបាក)
concepts.summary: Propositions, implication P => Q, contrapositive ~Q => ~P, and De Morgan's laws.
concepts.body: A proposition P is a declarative statement that is either true (T) or false (F). The implication P => Q is false ONLY when P is true and Q is false; its negation is P and ~Q, and its contrapositive ~Q => ~P is logically equivalent to P => Q.

concepts.title: Set Operations, Radicals & Absolute Value Intervals (ប្រមាណវិធីលើសំណុំ រ៉ាឌីកាល់ និងតម្លៃដាច់ខាត)
concepts.summary: Inclusion-exclusion n(A U B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A cap B), sqrt(A^2) = |A|, and |x - a| <= r.
concepts.body: For finite sets A and B, n(A U B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A cap B). For any real A, sqrt(A^2) = |A|. On the real number line, |x - a| <= r (for r >= 0) represents the closed interval [a - r, a + r], while |x - a| >= r represents (-inf, a - r] U [a + r, +inf).

prerequisites: Arithmetic operations on fractions and powers

formulas.name: De Morgan's Laws & Principle of Inclusion-Exclusion
formulas.expression: \overline{A \cup B} = \overline{A} \cap \overline{B}, \quad n(A \cup B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A \cap B)

variables.n(A): Cardinality (number of elements) of set A

examples.problem: Solve the absolute value inequality |2x - 5| <= 3 and express the solution as an interval.
solution_steps: Step 3: Divide by 2: 1 <= x <= 4, so x in [1, 4].

examples.problem: In a class of 45 students, 28 study English, 22 study French, and 10 study both. How many students study neither language?
solution_steps: Step 1: Apply inclusion-exclusion: n(E U F) = n(E) + n(F) - n(E cap F) = 28 + 22 - 10 = 40.
Step 2: Subtract from total students: 45 - 40 = 5 students study neither.

exercises.prompt: Simplify the radical expression 4 / (sqrt(7) - sqrt(3)) - sqrt(28).
hints: Multiply the fraction by the conjugate (sqrt(7) + sqrt(3)) / (sqrt(7) + sqrt(3)) and note sqrt(28) = 2*sqrt(7).
Require x + 4 >= 0 and split into 3x - 2 = x + 4 or 3x - 2 = -(x + 4).

solution_steps: Step 1: Identify domain conditions (e.g., radicands >= 0, right-hand side of |u| = v is >= 0).
Step 2: Apply set laws, conjugate rationalization, or absolute value equivalence.
Step 3: Write the final solution in interval or set notation.

common_misconceptions.text: Writing sqrt(x^2) = x instead of sqrt(x^2) = |x| when x is negative.
common_misconceptions.correction: The principal square root is always non-negative, so sqrt((-5)^2) = |-5| = 5.

common_misconceptions.text: Negating the implication P => Q as ~P => ~Q.
common_misconceptions.correction: P => Q is false only when P is true and Q is false, so ~(P => Q) is (P and ~Q).

subject: Mathematics
subtopic: Polynomial Division, Bezout's Theorem, Discriminant, Vieta's Formulas & Quadratic Inequalities
text: MoEYS Grade 10 Mathematics Chapters 3–4: Polynomials (ពហុធា), Quadratic Equations (សមីការដឺក្រេទី២), and Vieta's Formulas (ទ្រឹស្តីបទវីយ៉ែត). Covers Euclidean division of polynomials, Bezout's remainder theorem R = P(a), Horner's synthetic division, solving ax^2 + bx + c = 0 via discriminant Delta = b^2 - 4ac and reduced discriminant Delta' = b'^2 - ac, Vieta's sum S = x_1 + x_2 = -b/a and product P = x_1 x_2 = c/a, and sign tables of quadratic trinomials.

source.section: Polynomial Division, Bezout's Theorem, Discriminant, Vieta's Formulas & Quadratic Inequalities

metadata.topic_khmer: ពហុធា សមីការដឺក្រេទី២ និងទ្រឹស្តីបទវីយ៉ែត
metadata.subtopic_khmer: វិធីចែកពហុធា ទ្រឹស្តីបទបេហ្ស៊ូ ឌីស្គ្រីមីណង់ ទ្រឹស្តីបទវីយ៉ែត និងវិសមភាពដឺក្រេទី២
metadata.khmer_description: សិក្សាពហុធា ទ្រឹស្តីបទបេហ្ស៊ូ និងតារាងអរន័រ សមីការដឺក្រេទី២ ឌីស្គ្រីមីណង់ ទ្រឹស្តីបទវីយ៉ែត និងតារាងសញ្ញាត្រីធាដឺក្រេទី២។
metadata.starter_problem: x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0, \quad \text{find the roots and solve } x^2 - 5x + 6 < 0
learning_objectives: Apply Bezout's Remainder Theorem and Horner's scheme to factor polynomials
Solve quadratic equations ax^2 + bx + c = 0 using Delta = b^2 - 4ac and shortcut root rules (a + b + c = 0 or a - b + c = 0)
Use Vieta's formulas x_1 + x_2 = -b/a and x_1 x_2 = c/a to evaluate symmetric expressions of roots
Construct sign tables for quadratic trinomials and solve quadratic inequalities

concepts.title: Bezout's Remainder Theorem & Factor Theorem (ទ្រឹស្តីបទបេហ្ស៊ូ និងការដាក់ជាផលគុណកត្តា)
concepts.summary: Remainder of P(x) divided by (x - a) is P(a); (x - a) divides P(x) iff P(a) = 0.
concepts.body: For any polynomial P(x) and real number a, P(x) = (x - a)Q(x) + P(a). Thus a is a root of P(x) (P(a) = 0) if and only if (x - a) is a factor of P(x). The coefficients of Q(x) are quickly found using Horner's table.

concepts.title: Discriminant, Vieta's Formulas & Trinomial Sign Rule (ឌីស្គ្រីមីណង់ ទ្រឹស្តីបទវីយ៉ែត និងសញ្ញាត្រីធា)
concepts.summary: Delta = b^2 - 4ac, S = -b/a, P = c/a, and 'same sign as a outside the roots'.
concepts.body: For ax^2 + bx + c = 0 (a != 0), Delta = b^2 - 4ac. When Delta >= 0, the roots satisfy x_1 + x_2 = -b/a and x_1 x_2 = c/a. If Delta > 0, ax^2 + bx + c has the opposite sign of a strictly between x_1 and x_2, and the same sign as a outside [x_1, x_2].

khmer_terms.Polynomials, Quadratics & Vieta's Formul: ពហុធា សមីការដឺក្រេទី២ និងទ្រឹស្តីបទវីយ៉ែត

formulas.name: Quadratic Formula & Vieta's Relations
formulas.expression: \Delta = b^2 - 4ac, \quad x_{1,2} = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{\Delta}}{2a}, \quad x_1 + x_2 = -\frac{b}{a}, \quad x_1 x_2 = \frac{c}{a}

formulas.name: Bezout's Division Identity & Root Shortcut Cases
formulas.expression: P(x) = (x - a)Q(x) + P(a); \quad a + b + c = 0 \Rightarrow x_1 = 1, x_2 = \frac{c}{a}; \quad a - b + c = 0 \Rightarrow x_1 = -1, x_2 = -\frac{c}{a}

solution_steps: Step 1: Solve x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0: factor as (x - 2)(x - 3) = 0 => roots x_1 = 2, x_2 = 3.
Step 2: Since leading coefficient a = 1 > 0, the trinomial is negative strictly between the roots.
Step 3: Solution set is x in (2, 3).

examples.problem: Let x_1, x_2 be the roots of 2x^2 - 6x + 1 = 0. Compute x_1^2 + x_2^2 without finding the individual roots.
solution_steps: Step 1: By Vieta's formulas, S = x_1 + x_2 = -(-6)/2 = 3 and P = x_1 x_2 = 1/2.

exercises.prompt: Find the parameter m so that P(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 + mx + 6 is divisible by (x - 3).

hints: Find the roots of -2x^2 + 7x - 3 = 0 and remember a = -2 < 0.
solution_steps: Delta = 49 - 24 = 25, roots x_1 = 1/2, x_2 = 3. Since a = -2 < 0, trinomial >= 0 on [1/2, 3].
Step 1: Compute discriminant Delta = b^2 - 4ac (or check special coefficient sums a + b + c = 0, a - b + c = 0).
Step 2: Find roots or apply Vieta's sum S = -b/a and product P = c/a.
Step 3: For inequalities, construct the sign table using the sign of a.

common_misconceptions.text: Writing x_1 + x_2 = b/a instead of -b/a in Vieta's sum formula.
common_misconceptions.correction: Expanding a(x - x_1)(x - x_2) = ax^2 - a(x_1 + x_2)x + ax_1 x_2 shows x_1 + x_2 = -b/a.

common_misconceptions.text: Forgetting to reverse the sign table when the leading coefficient a is negative.
common_misconceptions.correction: Between the two roots, ax^2 + bx + c always has the sign opposite to a.

subject: Mathematics
subtopic: Domain, Even/Odd Functions, Parabola Vertex Form & Systems of Equations
text: MoEYS Grade 10 Mathematics Chapters 5–6: Functions (អនុគមន៍), Quadratic Parabolas (ប៉ារ៉ាបូល), and Systems of Equations (ប្រព័ន្ធសមីការ). Covers domain of definition, even and odd functions, variation tables, canonical form of a quadratic function y = a(x - h)^2 + k with vertex I(-b/(2a), -Delta/(4a)) and axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a), and solving 2x2 and 3x3 linear and linear-quadratic systems.

learning_objectives: Determine the domain of rational and radical functions and test parity (even/odd)
Rewrite y = ax^2 + bx + c in canonical form a(x - h)^2 + k and find its vertex, axis of symmetry, and extrema
Solve 2x2 and 3x3 linear systems using elimination/Cramer's rule and line-parabola intersection systems

concepts.title: Vertex & Canonical Form of a Parabola (ទម្រង់កាណូនិច និងកំពូលនៃប៉ារ៉ាបូល)
concepts.summary: y = a(x - h)^2 + k has vertex I(h, k) with h = -b/(2a) and k = -Delta/(4a).
concepts.body: Completing the square rewrites f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c as f(x) = a(x - h)^2 + k, where h = -b/(2a) and k = f(h) = -Delta/(4a). If a > 0, the parabola opens upward with minimum k at x = h; if a < 0, it opens downward with maximum k at x = h.

concepts.title: Line-Parabola Intersection & Linear Systems (ប្រសព្វរវាងបន្ទាត់និងប៉ារ៉ាបូល និងប្រព័ន្ធសមីការ)
concepts.summary: Set ax^2 + bx + c = mx + p and use discriminant Delta to count intersection points.
concepts.body: The intersections of parabola y = ax^2 + bx + c and line y = mx + p satisfy ax^2 + (b - m)x + (c - p) = 0. The line is secant (2 points) if Delta > 0, tangent (1 point) if Delta = 0, and disjoint (0 points) if Delta < 0.

formulas.name: Parabola Canonical Form & Vertex Coordinates
formulas.expression: y = ax^2 + bx + c = a(x - h)^2 + k, \quad h = -\frac{b}{2a}, \quad k = -\frac{\Delta}{4a}

examples.problem: Find the vertex, axis of symmetry, and minimum value of the parabola y = 2x^2 - 8x + 5.
examples.answer: Vertex I(2, -3), axis x = 2, minimum y_min = -3
solution_steps: Step 3: Since a = 2 > 0, the vertex is I(2, -3), axis is x = 2, and minimum value is -3.

examples.problem: Find the intersection points of the parabola y = x^2 - x - 2 and the line y = x + 1.
solution_steps: Step 1: Equate y-values: x^2 - x - 2 = x + 1 => x^2 - 2x - 3 = 0.
Step 2: Solve for x: (x + 1)(x - 3) = 0 => x = -1 or x = 3.
Step 3: Substitute into y = x + 1: for x = -1, y = 0; for x = 3, y = 4.

hints: Multiply the first equation by 2 and the second by 3, then add.

solution_steps: Step 1: Identify coefficients a, b, c of the quadratic function.
Step 2: Compute vertex coordinates h = -b/(2a) and k = f(h).
Step 3: Build the variation table according to the sign of a and plot key points.

common_misconceptions.text: Reading the vertex of y = a(x + 2)^2 - 3 as (2, -3) instead of (-2, -3).
common_misconceptions.correction: In a(x - h)^2 + k, (x + 2) means x - (-2), so h = -2.

subject: Mathematics
subtopic: Unit Circle, Fundamental Identities, Law of Sines, Law of Cosines & Triangle Area
text: MoEYS Grade 10 Mathematics Chapter 7: Trigonometry (ត្រីកោណមាត្រ) and Triangle Relations (ទំនាក់ទំនងក្នុងត្រីកោណ). Covers degree-radian conversion, the trigonometric unit circle, signs of trig functions in all four quadrants, fundamental identities sin^2(alpha) + cos^2(alpha) = 1 and 1 + tan^2(alpha) = 1/cos^2(alpha), Law of Cosines a^2 = b^2 + c^2 - 2bc cos A, Law of Sines a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C = 2R, and area formulas S = (1/2)bc sin A and Heron's formula.

concepts.title: Law of Cosines & Law of Sines (ទ្រឹស្តីបទកូស៊ីនុស និងទ្រឹស្តីបទស៊ីនុស)
concepts.summary: a^2 = b^2 + c^2 - 2bc cos A and a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C = 2R.
concepts.body: In any triangle ABC with sides a, b, c opposite angles A, B, C and circumradius R: the Law of Cosines generalizes the Pythagorean theorem to oblique triangles as a^2 = b^2 + c^2 - 2bc cos A, while the Law of Sines links sides and opposite angles to the circumdiameter 2R.

formulas.name: Law of Cosines, Law of Sines & Triangle Area
formulas.expression: a^2 = b^2 + c^2 - 2bc\cos A, \quad \frac{a}{\sin A} = \frac{b}{\sin B} = \frac{c}{\sin C} = 2R, \quad S = \frac{1}{2}bc\sin A = \sqrt{p(p-a)(p-b)(p-c)}

examples.problem: In triangle ABC, b = 5 cm, c = 8 cm, and angle A = 60 deg. Find side a and the area S of the triangle.
solution_steps: Step 2: Compute area: S = (1/2) * 5 * 8 * sin(60 deg) = 20 * (sqrt(3)/2) = 10*sqrt(3) cm^2.

exercises.prompt: Given cos(alpha) = -3/5 with pi/2 < alpha < pi, find sin(alpha) and tan(alpha).
hints: In Quadrant II, sin(alpha) > 0 and tan(alpha) < 0.

solution_steps: Step 1: Identify known sides and angles (SAS, SSS, ASA, or AAS).
Step 2: Use Law of Cosines for SAS/SSS or Law of Sines for ASA/AAS.
Step 3: Apply the appropriate area formula S = (1/2)bc sin A or Heron's formula.

common_misconceptions.text: Writing +2bc cos A instead of -2bc cos A in the Law of Cosines.
common_misconceptions.correction: The formula has a minus sign: a^2 = b^2 + c^2 - 2bc cos A (note that when A > 90 deg, cos A < 0 so -2bc cos A > 0).

subject: Mathematics
subtopic: 2D Vectors, Dot Product, Equations of Lines, Point-to-Line Distance & Circles
text: MoEYS Grade 10 Mathematics Chapters 8–9: 2D Vectors (វ៉ិចទ័រក្នុងប្លង់) and Plane Analytic Geometry (ធរណីមាត្រវិភាគក្នុងប្លង់). Covers Chasles' relation AB + BC = AC, midpoint and centroid coordinates, collinearity and orthogonality via 2D dot product u . v = x_1 x_2 + y_1 y_2, parametric and general equations of lines ax + by + c = 0, point-to-line distance d(M_0, L) = |ax_0 + by_0 + c|/sqrt(a^2 + b^2), and circle equations (x - a)^2 + (y - b)^2 = R^2.

concepts.title: Dot Product, Normal Vector & Point-to-Line Distance (ផលគុណស្កាលែ និងចម្ងាយពីចំណុចទៅបន្ទាត់)
concepts.summary: u . v = x_1 x_2 + y_1 y_2 = 0 for perpendicular vectors; line ax + by + c = 0 has normal n = (a, b).
concepts.body: Two vectors u(x_1, y_1) and v(x_2, y_2) are orthogonal iff x_1 x_2 + y_1 y_2 = 0. The line L: ax + by + c = 0 has normal vector n = (a, b), direction vector u = (-b, a), and distance from M_0(x_0, y_0) to L given by d(M_0, L) = |ax_0 + by_0 + c| / sqrt(a^2 + b^2).

examples.problem: Find the equation of the circle with center I(2, -1) that is tangent to the line L: 3x + 4y - 12 = 0.
solution_steps: Step 1: Radius R equals the distance from I(2, -1) to tangent line L: R = |3(2) + 4(-1) - 12| / sqrt(3^2 + 4^2) = |-10| / 5 = 2.

exercises.prompt: Find the center and radius of the circle x^2 + y^2 - 6x + 4y - 12 = 0.
hints: Complete the square for x^2 - 6x and y^2 + 4y.

solution_steps: Step 1: Extract coordinates of points, direction vectors, or normal vectors.
Step 2: Substitute into line, distance, or circle formulas.
Step 3: Simplify to standard or general form.

common_misconceptions.text: Taking R = 25 instead of R = sqrt(25) = 5 from (x - a)^2 + (y - b)^2 = 25.
common_misconceptions.correction: The right-hand side of the standard circle equation is R^2, so take its square root to get radius R.
